newsitem.title: FRANCE: African anti-narcotics police meet in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: African anti-narcotics police meet in Algeria.

text.p: Police from about 50 African countries gathered on Tuesday in Algiers to plot strategy to fight spreading drug abuse on the continent, Algeria's official news agency APS said.
"Drug trafficking has become a weapon used to annihilate people and destabilise states," Algeria's police chief Ali Tounsi was quoted by APS as telling the two-day meeting.
He urged police representatives to come forward with a policy to stem the narcotics trade in Africa.
International Interpol police chief Raymond Kendall said the gathering also aimed to display police solidarity with colleagues in Algeria fighting nearly six years of Moslem guerrilla violence.

About 60,000 people, including hundreds of policemen, have died in violence pitting government forces against Moslem rebels since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a huge lead.
Algeria is mainly a transit area for traffickers seeking to ship drugs to some rich African countries and into the European market.
Authorities have seized about 18 tonnes of drugs, mainly soft ones, in the past 10 years in Algeria. The main haul was six tonnes of hashish in 1992, according to official figures.

"Trafficking in cocaine and heroin drugs, which appeared early in the 1980s in Africa, has witnessed a lightning spread on the continent with involvement of more trafficking gangs," said Kendall, quoted by APS.
Africa needed an updated strategy to counter the drug tide by improving the continent's police cooperation, he added.
